summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 56% YoY to INR931 crore and PAT 32% to INR36 crore, while lead volumes fell on supply-chain disruption.
summary.overview: Revenue, EBITDA and PAT grew 56%, 30% and 32% YoY to INR931 crore, INR56 crore and INR36 crore, with EBITDA margin about 6%. Copper volumes more than tripled YoY to record levels and copper EBITDA per ton rose 66% to INR48,488. Lead volumes moderated as shipping delays via the Strait of Hormuz constrained scrap imports, and management chose to prioritise value-added products (85% of lead revenue), giving a record lead EBITDA of INR21,595 per ton. Management says demand is intact and the constraint is supply, not demand.

segments.name: Lead
segments.commentary: Volumes moderated due to supply constraints; value-added products were 85% of segment revenue. Export mix 55% of lead sales. Management guides sustainable lead EBITDA of INR18,000-20,000 per ton.

segments.name: Copper
segments.commentary: Production and sales volumes each rose more than 3x YoY to record levels (about 4,000 tonnes in the quarter per analyst); export mix 25%. Copper expected to be about 45% of FY27 revenue. Existing capacity about 75% utilised.

segments.name: Plastics
segments.commentary: Turned profitable in Q1 with net profit of about INR15 lakh on about 800 tonnes of volume.

segments.name: Aluminium
segments.commentary: Small production of about 200 metric tonnes in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Lead value-added mix for FY27 targeted at 65-70% (FY26 about 63%).
Lead EBITDA sustainable at INR18,000-20,000 per ton as volumes rise; Q1 INR21,595 was driven by 85% value-added mix.
Copper EBITDA per ton before value-addition guided above INR40,000 (earlier guidance INR35,000-40,000); cathode blended EBITDA guided INR60,000-65,000 per ton.
Management reiterated earlier FY27 lead volume guidance of about 1.25-1.3 lakh tonnes, saying it expects to close near that level, though it did not give a revised number.
2030 roadmap: over 15% volume growth, 20%+ CAGR in revenue and profitability, EBITDA margin above 8%, ROCE above 20%, over 60% revenue from value-added products.
FY27 capex about INR175 crore: maintenance INR20-25 crore, balance INR140-150 crore for copper plant. Management did not give volume guidance for FY27/FY28 by product yet.
capex_capacity: 36,000 tpa copper cathode plant at Thervoy Kandigai, Tamil Nadu, total investment about INR200 crore, funded from internal accruals; about INR25 crore spent so far.
Phase 1 (18,000 tpa) on track for commissioning in December 2026, trial runs in Q4 FY27; machine installation from end-September, Phase 2 (18,000 tpa) targeted for Q3 FY28.
Incremental 6,000 tpa copper recycling capacity commissioned in Q4 FY26 (copper recycling total about 12,000 tpa, in Andhra Pradesh); about 75% utilised. Target utilisation about 75% through FY27.
New 72,000 tpa lead (TKD) capacity utilisation below 50% because of the focus on value-added pure lead.
CRISIL upgraded outlook to A positive from A stable, rating reaffirmed.
demand_pricing: Management says there is no demand softness; the constraint is delayed shipments and supply-chain disruption.
Lead exports go mainly to Southeast Asia, not Europe; Middle East procurement below 5% of sourcing, with the main issue being shipping routes via the Strait of Hormuz.
Lead sourcing about 97% international in Q1; domestic prices were too high for profitable domestic buying, though management has started looking at domestic procurement.
Copper pricing was supported by tight availability, enabling a premium on copper sales.
Copper sourcing: mostly imports, with plans for 25-30% domestic sourcing going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Can lead volumes reach the 1.25-1.3 lakh tonne FY27 guidance given the current run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of closing up to the committed numbers but will see how supply chains evolve over the next 1-2 months; no revision given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there demand softness in lead, given exposure to Western and Middle East markets?
qa_highlights.answer: No demand softness; exports are mainly Southeast Asia. Only supply delays are affecting volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 16% YoY and 44% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Logistics is a small part; the major driver is fuel prices and some additive prices that rose over the last three months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the record lead EBITDA per ton one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a sustainable level is INR18,000-20,000 per ton; Q1 was high because of the 85% value-added mix.

qa_highlights.question: Capex split for FY27 of about INR175 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance INR20-25 crore; the balance of INR140-150 crore is for the new copper plant.

qa_highlights.question: Copper EBITDA per ton outlook before value addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects above INR40,000 per ton going forward, aided by capacity efficiencies and a premium in the current tight market.

qa_highlights.question: EPR credits and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: EPR benefit minimal this quarter as most purchases were imports; unmonetised EPR credits remain on the books. Working capital not stretched because payments are made about a week before arrival at port.

risks_watch: Lead volume shortfall from shipping disruption (Strait of Hormuz) could put the 1.25-1.3 lakh tonne FY27 guidance at risk; monthly production fell in May and early June.
Cost inflation from fuel and additive prices, with other expenses up 44% QoQ.
Copper cathode commissioning slipping beyond December 2026 would delay margin uplift; the cathode blended EBITDA of INR60,000-65,000 per ton is not yet proven.
Copper scrap security as global supply tightens and more countries retain scrap; reliance on imports for most copper sourcing.
Lead EBITDA per ton could normalise toward INR18,000-20,000 as the value-added mix falls from 85%.
Lead volumes fell sharply YoY, with analysts noting a much steeper decline than a competitor; management declined to comment.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the copper ramp-up and margins, but noticeably cautious and vague on lead volumes, where it repeatedly said it would wait 1-2 months before giving a firm view. Several answers were defensive or repetitive when pressed on FY28 copper volumes and recycling capacity.
key_quotes: We have started FY27 on a strong footing with Q1 FY27 revenue, EBITDA and PAT growing at 56%, 30% and 32% year -on-year, respectively.

While lead production and sales volumes moderated during the quarter, it was a conscious strategic decision to prioritize value-added products amidst supply chain disruption and production constraints that enabled us to achieve our highest ever lead EBITDA per ton of INR21,595.
So we can safely guide above 40,000 would be for the part which was earlier, 35,000 to 40,000.
There's no demand softening, but there has been only supply chain delays because of which the whole issues have been -- volumes have been lower and all of those.
Our commitment on starting the trial production was December 2026 and not September 2026.

growth.why: Q1 revenue +56% YoY with copper volumes more than tripling; management guides copper EBITDA above INR40,000/t pre-value-addition for FY27 and 80-90% utilisation of the 36kt cathode plant in FY28, backed by the Thervoy Kandigai plant (Phase 1 due Dec 2026) but lead FY27 volume guidance was not revised and lead volumes are constrained by shipping delays.
